feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Iteration 0 (±0.02 m spread, 12 mm footprint) gave 100% off-track failure, one line-loss event per trial and max_error about 0.061 m, just past the 0.06 m off-track limit, which is the binding constraint (the body term is 0.0425 m). Iteration 1 (±0.03 m spread, 12 mm footprint) reproduced those metrics exactly to four decimals on all three tracks, so it gives no evidence that spread alone matters, and it may be a duplicate run. Your 16 mm footprint change is the next test. Do not read an outcome into it yet. Next-race rules: (a) if line_loss_events fall to zero on the s-bend and slalom but max_error still reaches about 0.06 m, the limit is steering response, not visibility, so the next change is gain (kp near 3.0 on the same geometry) rather than more geometry; (b) if line loss persists with the 16 mm footprint, the sensors still do not reach far enough, so widen the spread to ±0.04 m (keep 5 sensors) and scale the weights to match; (c) if the robot completes but steering_oscillation is high on the slalom, reduce the forward lead to y = 0.03 m, changing nothing else. If the new race matches iterations 0 and 1 exactly again, stop changing geometry and check the data pipeline first.
requested_changes: Test sensor_size 0.016 m at the ±0.03 m spread (same positions, lead y = 0.05 m) to extend tape visibility by about 2 mm per side. Iteration 1 at 12 mm reproduced iteration 0 exactly, so the footprint is the first lever to isolate.
If line_loss_events stay above zero with 16 mm, widen the spread to ±0.04 m (x = -0.04, -0.02, 0, 0.02, 0.04) with weights scaled to x/0.02 (-2.0, -1.0, 0, 1.0, 2.0), keeping sensor_size 0.016 m.

If the robot completes but steering_oscillation is high on the slalom, test forward lead y = 0.03 m with the spread and footprint fixed, to isolate the lead effect. Do not change the lead before the footprint result is known.
